script: [Warm greeting at the door. Light, genuine — let them settle in.]
Welcome, come in. Make yourself comfortable. How are you doing today?
[Reference their pre-session forms if returned.] I had a chance to review what you sent over — thank you for taking the time with that.
Tell me a bit more about what brings you in today. When did this first start?
[Listen. Observe. Verify. Empathize. Their words, their filter, not yours.]
[Use open-ended questions first to let them reveal their frame, then anchor with closed-ended confirmations: 'So that means... yes?']
[Articulate their issue back to them clearly — this builds credibility, rapport, and belief.]
So if I understand correctly, what you are looking for is... [restate their goal in concrete, daily-life terms].
What does success look like for you? In your daily life, what would be different?
[Define a clear, measurable goal together.]

prompter: Environment check: chair right, water offered, temperature fine, phone silenced.
Normalize nerves about 'this weird thing called hypnosis' - most people wonder; that's normal.
One more light-humor beat - shoulders down, a smile, maybe a small laugh.
Posture preview: feet flat, hands resting - nothing to do yet, just settle.
Hold the axis all session: Physicals need to FEEL hypnosis; Emotionals need to feel UNDERSTOOD.
One easy breath together.
Transition line: 'Before we begin, let me tell you what hypnosis actually is...' -> Step 1.
check: Environment/comfort checked out loud
Nerves normalized without over-talking
E/P axis consciously held (feel it vs feel understood)
Client visibly settled (shoulders, breath, smile)
Clean bridge into the pre-induction talk
script: Before we get started, is there anything you need? Water? Restroom?
Go ahead and get comfortable in the chair. Feet flat on the floor. Hands resting on your thighs.
[Observe their posture, breathing rate, and comfort level. Match your breathing to theirs initially.]
Good. We are going to have a great session today.

drills.name: Pre-Induction Talk
prompter: Hypnosis is a natural, everyday state (movies, daydreams, falling in love) - narrow focus that relaxes the filter so negatives can become positives.
Deep sleep = cue words, not sleep. Aware throughout - maybe hyper-aware - you hear the room, stay in control, can't get stuck.
Not a truth serum; nothing you wouldn't do or say wide awake.
Suggestions serve YOUR stated conscious goals - nothing else.
Mind may wander - the subconscious knows when to return to my voice.
Light, heavy, tingly, or simply calm - whatever you feel is right for you.
Wondering if you're hypnotized is usually the sign you are.
Do-WITH process, not do-to. Your imagination and participation are the engine.
Link to their goal; today we start building the new associations.
Testing shows me how you take information in - can't pass or fail, so don't help, don't hinder.
Authority + hope: they ARE suggestible; this will work for them.
Ask for questions - if none: 'Good, because some people think...' and clear the top myths anyway.
Close forward: most people leave the first session feeling better already - the change has begun.
check: Dispelled myths (sleep, control, stuck, truth serum)
Set expectations (aware, wandering, sensations vary)
Framed do-with + participation
Linked hypnosis to the client's stated goal
Framed testing as no-pass/no-fail
Used the 'Good, because some people think...' follow-up or answered questions fully
Closed with the change-has-begun expectation
script: Before we begin the hypnosis portion, I want to explain what hypnosis is and what it is not.
Hypnosis is a natural state you already enter several times a day — when you drive past your exit, when you get lost in a movie, or when you drift off just before sleep.
All hypnosis is self-hypnosis. I am simply a guide. You are always in control and can open your eyes at any time.
You cannot get stuck in hypnosis. It is impossible. If I left the room, you would simply open your eyes on your own.
You will hear everything I say. You will remember everything. This is not sleep — it is a focused, heightened state of awareness.
I will not make you do anything you do not want to do. Nothing I suggest will go against your moral or ethical beliefs.
What I need from you is your willingness to follow simple instructions and your permission to guide you. That is all it takes.

drills.name: Theory of Mind
prompter: Primitive area at the base - survival. Fight = pushing through daily stress; Flight = withdrawing, escaping, taking time out.
60,000+ message units a day pour in (mind, body, environment) - overload is the doorway we'll use.
Ages 0-8: everything accepted as absolute truth; programming forms, positive and negative.
Everyday example pair: foods we love vs refuse, affection vs punishment - knowns we believe are true.
Those known associations = subconscious, about 88 percent of mind power.
Critical mind above - a filter and protector of the knowns.
Conscious mind on top - logic, reasoning, decisions, analysis, and willpower ('the one that quits when you need it') - about 12 percent.
Their change-attempt: thought travels down, filter checks the old programming, resists, blocks - same pattern repeats.
Hypnosis walks that same thought past the filter - a door opens, direct access - positive suggestion installs the new pattern.
I work the 88, you work the 12 - together 100.
Bridge: and the way we begin is by testing your suggestibility.
check: All zones named in order (primitive, 0-8, subconscious 88, critical filter, conscious 12)
Client's actual issue slotted into the flow
Blocked-change loop explained with the filter resisting
Hypnosis-bypass explanation landed
88/12 partnership close delivered
Bridged into suggestibility testing
Fight vs flight defined in daily-life terms
script: Let me draw something for you. Imagine your mind as a circle. The top portion, roughly twelve percent, is your conscious mind — the analytical, critical part that makes decisions, reasons through problems, and judges information.
The larger portion below, roughly eighty-eight percent, is your subconscious mind. This is where your habits, emotions, memories, and automatic behaviors live.
Between these two parts is a thin barrier called the critical mind. Think of it like a filter or gatekeeper. Its job is to compare new information against what you already believe.
When new information matches your existing beliefs, the critical mind lets it through. When it conflicts, the critical mind rejects it. This is why willpower alone rarely works for lasting change.

Hypnosis temporarily relaxes this critical mind, allowing positive suggestions to reach the subconscious directly. Once accepted at the subconscious level, the change becomes automatic — like updating the operating system rather than fighting with the apps.
Your issue lives in that eighty-eight percent. We are going to communicate directly with it today.

drills.name: Arm-Raising Induction
prompter: Setup: upright, feet flat, arm and hand ON the table - note WHICH arm and word everything to match. Glasses off, no gum.
Pre-check the movement: have them raise the hand to the forehead once - checks mechanics AND infers the arc the hand will travel.
Take away verbal responses now - answers go non-verbal (removing speech adds overload = more message units).
Capture the arm: look elbow-to-fingertips, close eyes, hold the picture - nod when it's clear.

Suggestibility questions with direct eye contact (sleep-walk/talk, waking unable to move, replaying arguments, lemon-mouth, visualize?, imagine?) - weight the last two; if 'no' to visualize, downshift to 'imagine/conceptualize' so no one fails.
E/P tell in the RISE: Physical Suggestible's hand rises led by the WRIST; Emotional Suggestible's rises straighter OUT from the arm - read it live.
Frame: 'I will notice the changes before you do - when YOU notice, nod yes.'
Physio nods: breathing deepens (more oxygen)... lips-throat-mouth dry, urge to swallow (natural, normal)... eye flutter = first stage.
Conversion: elbow pressing comfortably, down the forearm, wrist, fingertips - lighter and lighter, feather, then lighter still; small pulling or jerking twitches are the start - name them.
Misdirection interleave: other hand heavier against the leg, feet pressing the floor, back on chair, rhythm of breath - 4th NOD when they feel the weight difference.
Ownership frame: 'you're creating that sensation' - their skill, not yours.
E-clients: allowing, tendency, permission, you choose, peaceful, safe, greater sense of control. P-clients: direct - it IS lifting.
Inference boost: many powerful balloons tied around that wrist - floating.
Movement -> directive: lifting, rising, twisting, turning, palm and fingertips inward, upward and inward; head-to-hand or hand-to-head - let them choose; bicep tightening.
Head-to-hand close (P3): head grows heavy, drops to meet the rising hand - close the gap both ways. Steer to the BROW, not the eyes (avoid finger-poke).
Repeat the weave until the hand is about six inches from the face.
'The moment you make skin contact, nod - peak of suggestibility, hypnotic sleep.' Contact + nod -> SNAP (or touch forehead) -> Deep Sleep.
PHS anatomy, immediately: cue words + for the purpose of hypnosis + WITH YOUR PERMISSION + quickly, calmly, deeply + the body relaxes.

Depth read after the escape (eyes under lids): hypnoidal (up-down/REM) -> cataleptic (side-to-side) -> somnambulism (roll up, whites show; amnesia 30/60/80% by stage). Emotional may be deep yet feel light - trust the eyes.
Repetition target: the 'deep sleep' + PHS pair is given 6-8 times across the first session (peak + after each deepener).

Language matched to E/P mode; escalated only after movement

Depth read from the eye signs after the escape
script: I would like you to sit comfortably with both feet flat on the floor. Place your hands on your thighs. If you are wearing glasses, please remove them. If you have gum, please discard it.

Now I would like you to raise your right arm and bend it at the elbow, placing the palm of your hand in front of your face, about ten inches away, with your fingers pointing upward and above eye level.
Good. Now stare at your middle finger and take a deep, comfortable breath. On the exhale, notice how your fingers may begin to separate — wider and wider, further and further apart.
Now I am going to ask you a few questions. Rather than answering out loud, just nod your head yes or no. From this point forward, all your answers will be non-verbal.

Have you ever been driving and missed your exit? Have you ever been so absorbed in a movie that you forgot where you were? Have you ever replayed a conversation in your mind, wishing you had said something different?
Can you visualize your arm as it rests in front of you right now? Can you see every detail — the texture of the skin, the shape of each finger? Hold that image clearly.
Now I want you to notice something. I will notice the changes happening in your body before you do. When you notice them yourself, simply nod yes to let me know.
As you continue to focus on your hand, your breathing is beginning to deepen. You are taking in more oxygen. When you notice your breathing getting deeper, nod yes.
And as your breathing deepens, you may notice your lips and throat becoming dry. There may be an urge to swallow. That is perfectly natural — it means you are relaxing. When you notice this, nod yes.
Your eyelids may begin to flutter. This rapid movement is a natural sign that you are entering the first stages of hypnosis. When you notice this fluttering, nod yes.

Now notice that one hand feels heavier against your leg while the other hand, the one in front of your face, feels lighter. As if I were placing a feather beneath it. When you feel this difference in weight, nod yes.
That lightness is growing now. Your hand is becoming lighter and lighter. As if a gentle current of warm air were lifting it upward. You are creating this sensation. This is your ability.
Lighter and lighter, lifting and rising. Your hand is beginning to move — lifting, rising, turning slightly inward. Your palm and fingertips are rotating gently upward and inward toward your face.
Your hand continues to lift and rise, moving closer and closer to your face. Whether your head comes down to meet your hand or your hand rises to meet your face, allow it to happen naturally.
The moment you make skin contact — the moment your hand touches your forehead — give me a nod. At that instant you will reach your peak of suggestibility and enter the hypnotic state.
[Wait for contact and nod.] Deep Sleep.

Each and every time I suggest the words Deep Sleep to you, for the purpose of hypnosis and with your permission, you will enter this state of hypnosis very quickly, calmly, and deeply, and the physical body will relax.

drills.name: 5-to-0 Deepening Count
prompter: Hand gently back down to rest.
Frame: each count carries you deeper.
5 going down... 4 physical release... 3 emotional calm...
2 mental relaxing... 1 deeper and deeper...
0 -> SNAP -> Deep Sleep.
Repeat the PHS.
check: Each number carried its distinct meaning (physical / emotional / mental)
Pace slow and even
Snap + deep sleep on zero
PHS repeated
script: Now you can gently allow your hand to float back down to rest comfortably on your lap.
And as I count from five down to zero, each number will carry you deeper into this comfortable, heavy relaxation.
Five — going down now, deeper and deeper. Your body is beginning to let go.
Four — physically releasing, every muscle softening.
Three — emotionally calm, peaceful, at ease.
Two — mentally quiet, the inner dialogue fading.
One — deeper and deeper, drifting down.
Zero — [snap] — Deep Sleep.

Each and every time I suggest the words Deep Sleep to you, for the purpose of hypnosis and with your permission, you will enter this state of hypnosis very quickly, calmly, and deeply, and the physical body will relax.

And — Deep Sleep. [Snap.] Twice as deep.
Open your eyes.
And — Deep Sleep. [Snap.]
Open your eyes.
And — Deep Sleep. [Snap.] Twice as deep.

Each and every time I suggest the words Deep Sleep to you, for the purpose of hypnosis and with your permission, you will enter this state of hypnosis very quickly, calmly, and deeply, and the physical body will relax.

drills.name: Heavy/Light Deepener
prompter: Context: this version deepens an existing state (variants double as test or secondary induction).
Arms out at shoulder height - demonstrate with your own arms.
One palm up; other hand sideways, thumb to ceiling. Eyes close.
Heavy book on the open palm pressing down.
Many powerful balloons tied to the thumb pulling up.
Let the arms respond - watch a few moments.
Release both ideas, arms gently to the lap - Deep Sleep.
Repeat the PHS.
check: Demonstrated the arm positions yourself
Direction (down) and inference (up) both delivered
Allowed silent response time
Clean release + deep sleep
PHS repeated
script: Now I would like you to open your eyes and put both arms out in front of you at shoulder height, just like this. [Demonstrate.]
Good. Now one palm is facing upward, and the other hand is positioned with the palm facing inward and the thumb pointing straight up toward the ceiling. Go ahead and close your eyes.
Now imagine that I am placing a heavy bag of sand on the open palm. Feel it pressing downward. Heavy and solid, pressing your hand down.
And on your other thumb, imagine I am tying many powerful helium balloons. Feel the gentle upward pull, lifting your thumb higher and higher.
[Pause and observe — let the arms respond naturally for several seconds. Note which direction each arm moves.]
Good. Now you can release both of those ideas. Let go of the weight and the balloons. Allow your arms to relax and gently come down to rest on your lap.
Deep Sleep. [Snap.]

Each and every time I suggest the words Deep Sleep to you, for the purpose of hypnosis and with your permission, you will enter this state of hypnosis very quickly, calmly, and deeply, and the physical body will relax.

drills.name: Progressive Relaxation
prompter: Transition to recliner if still at desk — guide them while maintaining trance: 'remain in this relaxed state as you move.'
Recording note: this is usually where the client recording starts.
Permission frame: rhythm of breath, letting me guide you.
Top of head down: scalp, forehead, temples, eyelids, cheeks, jaw.
Outside-sounds reframe: everyday sounds send you deeper.
Neck, shoulders soften; arms to fingertips.
Chest opens, releases what no longer serves; solar plexus and belly unwind.
Breathing deep, gentle, rhythmic - drowsy daydream feeling.
Hips and pelvis release; thighs large-to-small muscles, knees, shins, calves.
Ankles, heels, arches, every toe - maybe tingling.
Terminal count 5 to 0 - zero -> SNAP -> Deep Sleep.
Repeat the PHS.
check: Recliner transition smooth (if applicable) — trance maintained
Recording started (or noted) before beginning
Permission frame delivered (rhythm of breath, giving permission)
Head-to-toe order unbroken (scalp -> forehead -> temples -> eyelids -> cheeks -> jaw)
Outside-sounds reframe included (everyday sounds deepen relaxation)
Neck and shoulders softened; arms traced to fingertips
Chest opens + solar plexus + belly area addressed (releasing what no longer serves)
Breathing deepens language: drowsy, sleepy, daydreaming
Hips -> thighs (large to small muscles) -> knees -> shins -> calves
Ankles -> heels -> arches -> toes with tingling sensation cue

script: [Transition: if the client is still in the desk chair, guide them to the recliner now. 'In a moment I am going to have you stand and move to the recliner. You will remain in this deeply relaxed state as you do. When you are settled, we will continue even deeper.' Wait for them to settle, adjust the footrest, offer a blanket.]
[Recording note: this is where the client recording typically begins.]
Now as you relax in your chair, you feel the rhythm of your own breathing. You feel connected inside. You are giving yourself permission to allow me to guide you.

Now bring your attention to the very top of your head. Allow a sense of relaxation to wash down over your scalp, across your forehead, your temples, your eyelids, and your cheeks. Allow your jaw to soften and relax.

Pay no attention to any outside sounds except the sound of my voice. These outside sounds are simply the everyday sounds of life. They cannot distract you or disturb you. In fact, they tend to relax you even further, allowing you to go deeper into this comfortable state.
As this calm continues spreading, let it release through your neck, softening all the muscles along the way, flowing through your shoulders, letting them drop and settle.

Now allow this sense of ease to continue down through your upper arms, past your elbows, through your forearms, releasing any tension from your wrists, your hands, and all the way to the very tips of your fingers.

And now this wave of relaxation moves into your chest, helping to open it, letting go of anything that no longer serves you. Down through your solar plexus and your stomach, bringing a deep sense of unwinding and release.
Your breathing is becoming very deep, gentle, and rhythmic. And a drowsy, sleepy, daydreaming feeling takes over. Letting go. Drifting down. Deeper and deeper.

Allow that calming sensation to continue through your hips, releasing any remaining tension. Down through your thighs, relaxing every muscle from the largest to the smallest. Through your knees, your shins, and your calves.
And as this peaceful feeling reaches your ankles, your heels, your arches, and loosens every single one of your toes to the very tips — perhaps you notice a gentle tingling sensation.
And now as I count down from five to zero, each number represents a deeper level of relaxation. You feel the body letting go even more with every count.
Five — letting go. Four. Three. Two. One. Zero — [snap] — Deep Sleep.

Each and every time I suggest the words Deep Sleep to you, for the purpose of hypnosis and with your permission, you will enter this state of hypnosis very quickly, calmly, and deeply, and the physical body will relax.

drills.name: Staircase Deepener
prompter: Place them at the top of a beautiful staircase - ten steps down (their scene, not yours).
Each step down doubles the relaxation - describe texture, light, handrail.
Count the steps down slowly, weaving deeper-with-every-step.
Adaptations: elder -> gentle garden path instead of stairs; child -> playground slide with a 3-count.
At the bottom: a place of complete comfort - Deep Sleep.
Repeat the PHS if first session.
check: Scene matched to the client (stairs / path / slide)
Step count paced with deepening language
Sensory detail present (not bare counting)
Bottom anchored to comfort + deep sleep
PHS repeated (first session)
script: Now I want you to visualize or imagine that you are standing at the top of a beautiful staircase. It is well-lit, with sturdy and smooth handrails, and it has twenty steps leading down to a comfortable landing below.
You have a sense of knowing that with each step downward, you will deepen your state of relaxation even more. Each step carries you further into comfort and peace.
So now, with your left foot you step down to nineteen, and your right foot follows at eighteen.
Twice as deep at seventeen. Sixteen. Feeling yourself deeply relax. Fifteen. Fourteen. Thirteen.
Twice as deep at twelve. Eleven. Ten.
Letting go at nine. Eight. Twice as deep at seven. Six. Five.
Deeper still at four. Three. Two. One. Zero — Deep Sleep.

Each and every time I suggest the words Deep Sleep to you, for the purpose of hypnosis and with your permission, you will enter this state of hypnosis very quickly, calmly, and deeply, and the physical body will relax.

drills.name: Suggestions (Literal + Inferred)
prompter: Deliver at least one INFERRED line: imagine / picture / consider / you may find...
Deliver at least one LITERAL line: you are... each day you...
Say it -> See it (their scene) -> Feel it (body registers).
Keep a memorized pair per issue (confidence: belonging-in-the-room inferred / each-day-stronger literal).
Permissive coda: no rush - unfolding naturally, with each breath.
Optional: venting-dream suggestions here if dream therapy is part of the plan.
Identity close: not becoming someone new - remembering who you've always been.
check: Clean inferred example delivered
Clean literal example delivered
Say-See-Feel arc complete
Lines traced to the client's goal (not generic)
Unhurried delivery
script: [Deliver suggestions tailored to the client's presenting issue. Include both inferred and literal language. Use the templates below as starting points — adapt the bracketed sections to the client's own words from intake.]
[--- TEMPLATE A: Vocational Confidence (presentations, interviews, performance) ---]
You may begin to notice, in the days and weeks ahead, that something is shifting inside. A quiet, steady confidence is building — naturally, effortlessly, in its own time.

And you can see yourself in that moment — standing in front of your colleagues, or sitting across the table in that meeting — and you feel a calm steadiness. Your voice is clear. Your thoughts are organized. You belong in that room.
Each day you grow stronger in this feeling. Each day it becomes more naturally a part of who you are.
[--- TEMPLATE B: Pain Comfort / Referral (adjunct to medical treatment) ---]
And as your body continues to relax, you are discovering something important — that you have more influence over your own comfort than you may have realized.

You can imagine a dial, from zero to ten, that represents the level of sensation in that area. And with each breath, you are gently turning that dial down. Not forcing it. Simply allowing your body to do what it already knows how to do — regulate, adapt, and find ease.
Each day, you find it easier to access this feeling of comfort. Your body remembers. Your subconscious remembers.
[--- TEMPLATE C: Avocational Performance (sports, creativity, focus) ---]
See yourself at the starting line — or on that stage, or at that desk — and notice how your body feels. Loose. Ready. Alert but calm. Every muscle knows its job.
When the moment comes, you do not think — you flow. The training is in your body. The preparation is complete. You simply trust yourself and let it happen.
And afterward, you feel that deep satisfaction of knowing you showed up fully. Not perfect — present. That is enough.
[--- COMMON CLOSE (use with any template) ---]
And your subconscious mind is absorbing these ideas now, integrating them, making them your own. There is no rush. This is unfolding at exactly the right pace for you.
Not becoming someone new — but remembering who you have always been.

[Optional: Venting dream.] And tonight, or in the nights that follow, you may have a dream — a cleansing dream — where any remaining tension or old patterns are simply released. You may or may not remember the dream. Either way is perfectly fine. When you awaken, you will feel refreshed and lighter.

5 - EYES OPEN, WIDE AWAKE.
Rapid repeat: 1-2-3-4-5 eyes open wide awake.

script: Now I am going to count from zero up to five. With each number you will become more alert, more awake, more refreshed, with a wonderful sense of well-being.

Two — becoming more physically aware, more mentally alert.
Three — coming up higher now, feeling wonderful.
Four — your eyes are beginning to open.
Five — eyes open, wide awake! Feeling alert, refreshed, and wonderful.
One, two, three, four, five — eyes open, wide awake!

script: [After counting the client out, allow them to orient for a moment. Then use this to verify the PHS is installed.]
Welcome back. How do you feel? [Brief check-in.]
Now I would like to verify something. Raise your arm and place the palm of your hand in front of your face, just as you did before. Stare at your middle finger.
Take a deep breath — and on the exhale, your fingers begin to separate once more. Separating, wider and wider.
As your fingers continue to separate, your hand is beginning to move closer to your face. Your breathing is deepening. Your eyelids are growing heavy.
When your hand comes all the way in to touch your face, give me a nod. The moment you make skin contact, your eyes will close and you will enter the hypnotic state.
[Wait for contact.] Deep Sleep. [Snap.]

Good. This tells us the connection is established. Each and every time I suggest the words Deep Sleep to you, for the purpose of hypnosis and with your permission, you will enter this state of hypnosis very quickly, calmly, and deeply, and the physical body will relax.
[Count them back out: 0-1-2-3-4-5, eyes open, wide awake.]

[Assign any behavioral tasks related to their presenting issue.]
If you have any questions between sessions, do not hesitate to reach out.
Schedule your next appointment on the way out. Consistency is important — we build on each session.
You did excellent work today. How are you feeling?

drills.name: Hand-to-Forehead Challenge
prompter: Use right after arm-raising, while the hand still rests at the forehead.
Unity image: hand and head as one piece of solid, beautiful marble.
Connected, comfortable, strong - the pressing feeling grows.
Challenge (paternal tone): you may try to pull the hand away - the more you try, the stronger it presses.
Let them try briefly; the failure deepens conviction.
Release the idea, hand gently to the lap - Deep Sleep.
Repeat the PHS.
check: Timed off the arm-raise (hand already at forehead)
Unity image built before any challenge
Challenge voiced in a firmer, paternal tone
Try-and-fail loop kept brief and safe
Clean release + deep sleep + PHS
script: [Use this immediately after the arm-raising induction, while the client's hand is already pressing against their forehead.]
Now as you continue to feel your hand pressing into your forehead, you have a very connected and comfortable sensation.

It is almost as though you can imagine yourself as a solid marble statue, with your hand and your head being one solid piece of beautiful marble. You have such a connected and strong feeling of your hand pressing into your forehead.
[Shift to a firmer tone.] And the feeling is so strong that you may try to pull your hand away, but the more you try, the stronger your hand presses into your forehead.
You may try and pull your hand away, but the more you try, the stronger your hand presses into your forehead.
[Allow a brief moment for them to test.] So, at five — your body relaxes. Four — your mind is letting go. Three — you emotionally feel calm. Two. One. Zero — Deep Sleep. [Snap.]

Each and every time I suggest the words Deep Sleep to you, for the purpose of hypnosis and with your permission, you will enter this state of hypnosis very quickly, calmly, and deeply, and the physical body will relax.
Now you can gently allow your hand to float back down to rest on your lap.

drills.name: Arm Rigidity Challenge
prompter: Arm straight out, make a fist.
Picture all the body's tension flowing into that arm.
Tighter and tighter, stiffer and stiffer as it floods in.
Steel bar from shoulder to wrist.
Count 5 to 0 building stiffness - at 0: the more you try to bend it, the stiffer it becomes.
Brief try; then release all tension, arm soft to the lap - Deep Sleep.
Repeat the PHS.
check: Fist + full-arm extension set first
Tension-transfer image before the count
5-to-0 stiffness count delivered
Try-to-bend paradox line landed
Full release verified (arm soft) + deep sleep + PHS
script: Now I would like you to put your arm straight out in front of you, making a fist.
I want you to picture all the tension in your body traveling into that arm. And the more it travels there, the tighter your arm becomes.
Feel it becoming tighter and tighter, stiffer and stiffer, with all the tension flooding into your arm.

Your arm is so stiff that it feels like a steel bar, all the way from your shoulder to your wrist. Becoming tighter and tighter, stiffer and stiffer, like a solid steel bar from your shoulder to your wrist.

Now at five — stiffer and stiffer. Four — tighter and tighter. Three — as stiff as a steel bar. Two. One. And zero — the more you try to bend it, the stiffer it becomes. The more you try to bend it, the stiffer it becomes.
[Allow a brief moment for them to test.] And now in a few moments, but not now, it will become as limp and relaxed as can be.
Three. Two. One. Release your arm to your lap. All the tension drops away. Any limiting beliefs dropping away. And with every breath you remember to let go of what no longer serves you.
And that is Deep Sleep. [Snap.]

Each and every time I suggest the words Deep Sleep to you, for the purpose of hypnosis and with your permission, you will enter this state of hypnosis very quickly, calmly, and deeply, and the physical body will relax.

drills.name: Eye Fascination (Secondary Induction)
prompter: Pick a spot on the ceiling - eyes looking up a bit, resting on that point.
Keep focusing without moving the eyes; wandering-and-returning is fine.
Match your speech to their breathing rhythm.
Bring awareness to the muscles around the eyes... the eyelids... what they feel like.
Heaviness builds; blinking increases; the blink-heavy loop.
Eyes prefer to close... closing... - Deep Sleep and deepen from there.
check: Spot placed above natural eye level
Breathing pace matched before deepening language
Eyelid-muscle awareness built gradually
Blink-heavy loop used (not rushed to close)
Close converted to deep sleep + deepener
script: From where you are sitting comfortably, I would like you to pick a spot on the ceiling above you, so that your eyes are having to look up slightly. Find that spot now and keep your eyes resting on it.
Just look at that point. Keep focusing on that spot without moving your eyes. And as you do, you can become aware of the muscles around your eyes — how they are holding your eyes in position.
You may [wait for blink] blink a bit more frequently now. That is right. And your breathing might get deeper as you relax.

As your eyes continue to rest on that spot, your mind focused on it, your eyelids may begin to feel heavy. Or your eyes may want to close. But I do not want you to close them just yet. Let them remain open.
And blinking [wait for blink], even more frequently now. You might wonder if that blink is slower than normal.
Many people find that as they begin to enter hypnosis, their focus becomes fuzzy. Their vision gets blurry. That spot may begin to waver, or change shape, or shift in color.
Your arms and legs are getting heavy. Your eyelids are getting heavier and heavier. When you are ready, you can allow your eyes to close.
[Pause — their eyes may already be closed.] And closing those eyes means you can relax now. It feels so good, so peaceful.
Breathing in for a moment, and breathing out, allowing the relaxation to double throughout your entire body. Going deeper and deeper.
Five — your body relaxes. Four — your mind is letting go. Three — feeling emotionally calm. Two. One. Zero — Deep Sleep. [Snap.]

drills.name: Auto Dual Induction
prompter: Alternative PRIMARY induction (101-5 item 8) - pulse focus + repeat-after-me. Glasses off, no gum.
Reserved for the Intellectual Suggestible (80%+ Emotional) who keeps talking/questioning themselves out - speaking aloud with 'I' makes them suggestible to themselves (101-4P).
BEFORE auto-dual, try to rescue a stalling arm-raise: (in person) lift the wrist, press the fingers gently back, 'when I release your hand, the fingers lift and rise' - release on 'lift'.
Or take the arm halfway up (in person) / have them lift it consciously, and keep the 'lighter and lighter' patter going.
If the hand starts sinking, go with it: 'when the hand touches the table, you reach the peak of your suggestibility.'
In person, hover slightly closer than comfortable during the pulse-find (adds message units).
Sit up straight, feet flat. Arm out; other index finger on that wrist - feel the pulse; nod when you have it.
Confirm: 'Are you sure?' then have them stare at the fingernail while holding attention on the pulse (dual focus).
Slow deep breath. Set the frame: 'I'll say phrases, you say each one out loud right after me' - wait for the nod.
Lead the five setup lines (enter hypnosis / for deep relaxation and self-control / count 5-0 / deeper each count / at zero deep asleep).
SPEED UP the descent, speaking slightly OVER them - this overload is the mechanism.
5 breathing deep-gentle-rhythmic... 4 eyelids heavy, drowsier... 3 every muscle-nerve-fiber relaxing...
2 arms-legs-whole-body relaxed... 1 eyelids closing, rhythmic... 0 -> Deep Sleep.

After 'deep sleep' -> Progressive Relaxation, use control-frame words (they need to feel in control): allowing the calming, because you choose to allow it, giving yourself permission, a greater sense of control, tendency, peaceful, safe.
Repeat the PHS.
check: Attempted at least one arm-raise rescue before resorting to auto-dual
Pulse found and confirmed ('are you sure?') before proceeding
Dual focus set (fingernail + pulse)
Repeat-after-me frame agreed with a nod
Five self-spoken setup lines delivered and echoed
Count accelerated with slight overlap (overload)
Control-frame language used in the post-induction relaxation
Zero -> deep sleep -> PHS
script: Now I would like you to raise both arms, elbows on the armrests, and make two fists.
I want you to stare directly between those two fists. Focus your eyes right between them.
As you stare between your fists, you may notice one fist beginning to feel lighter than the other. Allow that feeling.
And as one feels lighter, the other may feel heavier. One lifting, one pressing down.
Now I am going to count from eight down to one. With each count, the lighter hand continues to rise and the heavier hand continues to press down.
Eight — noticing the difference. Seven — one lighter, one heavier. Six — the separation growing.
Five — your eyes are becoming tired. Four — the lighter hand rising. Three — heavier and lighter.
Two — your eyelids growing heavy. One — and when you are ready, allow your eyes to close.
And as your eyes close, both hands can relax and come down to rest on your lap.
Deep Sleep. [Snap.]

Each and every time I suggest the words Deep Sleep to you, for the purpose of hypnosis and with your permission, you will enter this state of hypnosis very quickly, calmly, and deeply, and the physical body will relax.

drills.name: Guided Imagery (Secondary Induction)
prompter: Secondary induction (101-5 item 17). Breath focus; eyes close on the exhale of the 3rd/4th breath.
Fallback baked in: not everyone visualizes - imagine, think about, or conceptualize; use the other senses too.
Head-to-toe release: crown -> face/jaw -> shoulders -> arms/hands -> chest/back -> stomach -> hips -> legs -> toes.
Count backward 5-0 in their own mind with you; at 0 -> Deep Sleep.
The journey: meadow on a perfect day - earth underfoot, scent of nature, wildflowers.
A free-flying bird; gentle breeze through distant trees (multisensory).
A single beautiful tree on a hill; approach and take in its form and the leaf-sounds.
One leaf at the branch tip twists and turns, breaks free, glides down to rest at the base.
At the roots, a single blade of grass - persevered and strong through its own motivation.
Embed: 'the same way YOU are motivated' - take what we discussed, understand it, help yourself. Carry the feelings forward.
From here: give therapeutic suggestions, or deepen further.
check: Eyes closed on a breath exhale, not by command
Visualize/imagine/conceptualize fallback offered
Full head-to-toe release before the 5-0 count
Journey kept multisensory (sight, smell, sound, feel)
Leaf + blade-of-grass metaphor delivered with the motivation embed
Handed off to suggestions or a further deepener
script: Let us begin by focusing on your breath. Take a nice, easy breath through your nose. And then slowly release it through your mouth.
In your own words, in your mind, give yourself permission to allow me to guide you on this journey. On the exhale of your third or fourth breath, allow your eyes to close.
Although we cannot all visualize equally, we can all imagine. If you cannot see something as a picture, simply think about it, conceptualize it, or feel it. All of these work.

Let us start at the top of your head and gently work downward, releasing any pressure. Down over the facial muscles, the jaw releasing, the shoulders dropping, down your arms and hands, through the chest and back, the stomach and lower back, through the hips and all the way down to the tips of your toes.
Now count backwards with me in your mind. Five — moving into that wonderful imaginative space. Four. Three — even deeper. Two. One. And zero — Deep Sleep.
You feel the rhythm of your breath and feel yourself opening your imaginative mind.

Allow yourself to imagine a beautiful meadow on a perfect day. The temperature is exactly as you want it to be. You can feel the soft earth beneath your feet. Perhaps there is a sweet smell of wildflowers.
Walking through this meadow, you see a magnificent bird gliding across the sky — majestic and free. And you feel that same freedom inside yourself.
Ahead, at the top of a gentle hill, stands a single beautiful tree. As you approach, you hear the leaves rustling in a soft breeze. The sounds and smells and images create a deep feeling of ease.
Near the top of the tree, on one branch, there is a single leaf. You watch it twist and turn in the breeze. And something inside you knows it is about to let go.
And all at once the leaf breaks free, and the breeze carries it slowly — gliding down, back and forth, until it comes to rest near the base of the tree.
And beside it, a single blade of grass has persevered and grown strong. In the same way that you are finding your own strength and motivation. And that feels wonderful.

drills.name: Self-Hypnosis (Client Homework)
prompter: Teach this as a take-home tool (101-5 item 18). Client needs their three keywords first: physical, emotional, intellectual('DEEP SLEEP').
Physical keyword menu (pick ONE that resonates): heavy, floating, relaxation, lightness, loose, tingling, limp.
Emotional keyword menu (pick ONE): calmness, confidence, success, happiness, joy, contentment, peace.
Same three words every time (Law of Association) + daily practice builds momentum (Law of Repetition).
Frame the difference: hetero-hypnosis DISORGANIZES the critical mind to escape; self-hypnosis ORGANIZES it to bring in helpful info - it feels more present and connected.
Placement/safety: semi-comfortable with head supported; NOT in bed (unless for insomnia), NEVER while driving, and not when low/depressed with negative self-talk.
Semi-comfortable position; create an eye fascination - stare at a point above and in front.
Three breaths (in nose, out mouth, relax jaw); close eyes on the exhale of the third.
Top of head: repeat the PHYSICAL keyword to self; work down every body section, flowing with the physical feeling.
Count 5-0; at zero focus on the breath and repeat the EMOTIONAL keyword - really feel it.
Walk down a 20-step staircase; at the bottom say the intellectual keyword to self: DEEP SLEEP.
Give the prepared suggestions WITH feeling; repeat several times.
Count 0 up to 5: 'Eyes open, wide awake.' (Somnambulists may add 'to a completely non-suggestible state.')
check: Three personal keywords identified (physical / emotional / intellectual)
Keyword picked from the physical + emotional menus (not vague)
Hetero- vs self-hypnosis distinction explained (organize vs disorganize)
Placement/safety stated (not bed / driving / low mood)
Eye-fascination open + 3-breath close
Physical keyword body scan top-to-bottom
5-0 then emotional keyword, felt not just said
20-step staircase then 'deep sleep'
Suggestions delivered with feeling; clean 0-5 count out
script: Now I am going to teach you self-hypnosis, so you can practice this on your own between our sessions.
First, get into a semi-comfortable position. Not too comfortable — we do not want you falling asleep.
Create an eye fascination by staring at a point above and slightly in front of you.
Take three breaths — inhale through the nose, exhale through the mouth, relaxing the jaw. On the exhale of the third breath, allow your eyes to close.

Now focus on the top of your head. Repeat your physical keyword to yourself: [their chosen keyword]. Work down through every section of the body, repeating the physical keyword and flowing with that physical feeling of relaxation.
When you reach the bottom, count down from five to zero. At zero, focus on your breathing, then repeat your emotional keyword: [their chosen keyword]. Really try to feel it.
Then walk down a staircase of twenty steps in your imagination.
At zero, say your intellectual keywords to yourself: Deep Sleep.
Now give yourself the suggestions you have prepared. Feel the words. Feel the suggestions. Repeat them several times with feeling.
When you are ready, count from zero up to five. Tell yourself: eyes open, wide awake.
[If the client has somnambulistic tendencies, add: 'to a completely non-suggestible state.']
Practice this every day. The more you practice, the faster and deeper you will go each time.
Any questions about the self-hypnosis process?

drills.name: NLP: Rapport, Pace & Lead
prompter: Communication split: 7 percent words, 38 tonality, 55 body - work all three channels.
Match and mirror: posture, gesture size, breathing rhythm, tempo of speech.
Pace with truisms they can verify: my voice, the chair, the hands resting, the breath.
Then lead with a connector: and that means... which allows... so you can begin to...
Read sensory acuity live: skin tone, breathing rate and location, lower lip, eye focus, pupils.
VAK match: feed back their predicate system (see/look - hear/listen - feel/touch - or 'makes sense').
Resistance = lack of rapport, not a resistant client - flex the approach, not the person.
Map is not the territory: their words through THEIR filter; calibrate on behavior.
check: Mirrored at least two body-language channels
Three verifiable pacing statements before any lead
Lead delivered on a connector, accepted without resistance
Predicates matched to their favored system
One acuity shift noticed and used out loud
Reframed any resistance as a rapport signal to yourself
script: [Match the client's breathing rate for the first thirty seconds.]
[Mirror their posture subtly — cross the same leg, tilt your head the same direction.]
[Match their speaking pace and volume before gradually leading them to a calmer rhythm.]
[Use their exact words when reflecting back — do not paraphrase their emotional language.]
I understand what you mean when you say... [use their words]. That makes complete sense.
[Begin to slow your speech rate slightly — if they follow, rapport is established.]
[Deepen the breath you are modeling — if their breathing follows, you can begin to lead.]

drills.name: NLP: Well-Formed Outcome
prompter: Open: how is it possible they don't have it yet?
State it positive: what specifically do they WANT (not what they don't).
Sensory evidence: what will they see, hear, and feel when they have it?
Present tense, as-if-now; future-pace a dated scene.
Present situation (associated) vs outcome scene (dissociated first).
First step: if nothing else mattered, the very next action?
Self-initiated and self-maintained - are they in charge of the result?
Context: where, when, with whom - any drawbacks there?
Resources: have they or anyone they know done this before?
Ecology: good for them, for others, for the wider system?
check: Outcome stated in the positive
See-hear-feel evidence captured
First step named and concrete
Self-maintained ownership confirmed
Context and drawbacks explored
Ecology question asked
script: What specifically would you like to achieve? [Get concrete, sensory-based answer.]
How will you know when you have it? What will you see, hear, or feel that tells you things have changed?
Is this goal something that is within your control — something you can initiate and maintain yourself?
Where, when, and with whom do you want this? [Context and ecology check.]
What will you gain when you achieve this? And is there anything you might lose or give up?
What resources do you already have that can help? What additional resources do you need?
What is the first small step you can take?
On a scale of one to ten, how committed are you to making this change?

drills.name: Abreaction Handling
prompter: Definition (101-2P): an abreaction is an UNCONSCIOUS reaction to a therapeutic suggestion - a twitch, a sudden movement, a shift of affect.
First response: calmly give the SAME suggestion again and watch.
If the second time it does NOT abreact and is accepted - they released whatever was in the way. Continue.
If it abreacts AGAIN - make a note, move on, and know you may need more foundational work before returning.
Read the body: change of affect / softening = a healthy letting-go or release.
Erratic or sharp abreaction = fear present around that theme.
Constant movement = a possible trust issue - slow down, rebuild rapport and safety.
Never force the suggestion through; the abreaction is information, not failure.
Legal-language guard while re-wording: never 'cure' - use improve, modify, or positively change.
check: Recognized the abreaction as an unconscious response (not client resistance)
Re-delivered the same suggestion once and observed
Correctly branched (accept & continue vs note & move on)
Read the physical indicator (release / fear / trust)
Avoided forcing; treated it as information
script: [An abreaction is a sudden, strong emotional release during hypnosis. Stay calm — this is therapeutic, not dangerous.]
[Do NOT say 'calm down' or try to stop the emotion. Allow the release.]
That is right. Let it out. Let it go. Whatever you are feeling right now, it is safe to feel it here.
[If crying: offer a tissue without breaking the flow.] You are safe. I am right here with you.
This is your body and mind releasing something that has been held too long. This is healthy. This is healing.
[If the abreaction is intense, ground them:] Feel your feet on the floor. Feel the chair supporting you. You are here, in this room, and you are safe.
[Do NOT emerge them during an abreaction unless they request it. Let the wave pass naturally.]
[After the abreaction subsides:] Take a deep breath. How are you feeling now? [Pause.] Good. We can continue when you are ready.
[Note the abreaction in your session record — timing, trigger if known, resolution.]

drills.name: Inferred Rapport: Pace, Mirror & Permissive Frame
prompter: Match breathing rhythm before any verbal lead - count three cycles.
Mirror posture subtly: head tilt, hand position, weight shift.
Pre-induction for emotionals: 'You will hear sounds that seem louder than usual. Many thoughts will pass through your mind, even questions about whether you are hypnotized.'
Control frame: 'This is a do-with process, not a do-to process. A cooperative process.'
Normalize: 'Whatever you experience is right for you - some feel light, some heavy, some just calm.'
Pace with three verifiable truisms: 'You're here, sitting comfortably, you can hear my voice...'
Lead on a connector: '...and that means the part of you that wants this change is already at work.'
Use their predicates back: if they said 'I see what you mean' -> visual; 'I feel stuck' -> kinesthetic.
Permissive frame: 'you might notice,' 'perhaps,' 'you may find' - never 'you will.'
Name their affect back: 'I can see this matters to you' - verify, don't assume.
Emotional client axis: they need to feel UNDERSTOOD, not instructed.
Resistance = insufficient rapport. Flex the approach, not the client.
Close forward: 'And because of that...' - bridge to the induction.
check: Breathing rhythm matched before the first verbal lead
At least two body-language channels mirrored
Three verifiable truisms paced before leading
Permissive language throughout (no 'you will' commands)
Client's own predicates used in at least one lead
Emotional axis held (understood, not instructed)
Clean bridge into the induction

drills.name: Inferred Arm-Raising Induction (Permissive Lane)
prompter: Setup: arm on table, feet flat, glasses off, no gum. Lift arm to face 4x to preview the path.
Visualize: 'Look at your arm, elbow to fingertips - get a good picture - close your eyes.'
Suggestibility questions: sleep-walk? replay arguments? lemon? visualize? (Weight the last two.)
Physiology nods: breathing deeper -> nod. Lips dry, urge to swallow -> nod. Eye flutter under lids.
Permissive conversion: 'imagine your hand becoming lighter - very, very light - light as a feather.'
Ownership frame: 'as you begin to CREATE that sensation, it gives you a greater sense of control.'
Misdirection: 'at the same time your right hand feels heavier on your leg, feet pressing into the floor.'
Tie to breathing: 'with every breath, that sense of the left hand growing lighter and lighter.'
Allow, don't command: 'you may notice little pulling or tugging motions beginning.'
Double bind: 'I wonder whether it's the hand being drawn to the face, or the face to the hand, or both drawn together. I will let you decide.'
Power words for emotionals: lifting, rising, twisting, turning, lighter, upwards, inwards.
Never force the rise - if the hand is slow, pace it: 'a tendency to lift with each breath.'
If stalling: 'when the hand touches the table, you reach the peak of your suggestibility' (go-with).
Withhold closure: let the client close the gap at their own pace.
Skin contact + nod -> SNAP -> Deep Sleep.
PHS anatomy immediately: cue + purpose + permission + quickly/calmly/deeply + body relaxes.
Key vocabulary: allow, permit, imagine, drift, float, notice, gentle, tendency, choose, peaceful.
check: Permissive framing throughout (no direct 'it IS lifting' commands)
Balloon/helium imagery used for lightness
Ownership frame delivered ('you are creating')
Double bind offered (hand-to-face / face-to-hand / both)
Misdirection woven with heavy-hand imagery
Stalling handled with go-with reframe (not forced)
Closure withheld until client initiates
Skin contact -> snap -> deep sleep -> PHS

drills.name: Inferred Deepening: Eye Fascination + Permissive Staircase
prompter: Eye fascination (E-lane): spot on ceiling, gaze may drift and come back gently.
Build eyelid awareness gradually: 'you can begin to notice the small muscles around the eyes.'
Withhold closure: 'the eyelids may start to feel heavy... but not just yet.'
Blink-heavy loop: 'that blink is a little slower than normal' - pace the natural blinks.
Vision blur: 'the spot might waver, or blur, or seem to shift shape or color.'
Permissive close: 'when you are ready, you can let them close.'
Staircase (permissive variant): their scene, not yours - garden path, forest trail, beach steps.
Sensory detail per step: texture, light, scent, warmth - not just counting.
Pace language: 'with each step... drifting... settling... each one a little more comfortable.'
At the bottom: 'a place of complete comfort and safety - Deep Sleep.'
PHS repeated.
check: Eye fascination ran permissive (withhold closure, not command-close)
Blink-heavy loop observed and paced (not rushed)
Vision-blur suggestion offered as possibility
Close initiated by the client (not commanded)
Staircase scene chosen by the client's imagery
Sensory detail on at least three steps
Bottom anchored to comfort + deep sleep + PHS

drills.name: Inferred Suggestions: Permissive Therapeutic Language
prompter: Core principle: inferred suggestions imply change is happening rather than commanding it.
Permissive openers: 'you might find...', 'perhaps you notice...', 'you may begin to...'
Presupposition: 'as you continue to relax' (assumes they ARE relaxing).
Embedded commands within longer sentences: 'and I wonder if you can FEEL THAT COMFORT spreading.'
Truism chains: three observable truths, then the suggestion rides the yes-set momentum.
Say it -> See it -> Feel it: paint the outcome scene, then anchor it in the body.
Future-pace: 'and tomorrow, in that meeting, you might notice how calm your hands feel.'
Double bind: 'you can let this change happen quickly, or you can allow it to unfold gradually.'
Tag questions: 'that feels comfortable, doesn't it?' - lock in the acceptance.
Permissive coda: 'no rush - unfolding naturally, with each breath.'
Identity close: 'not becoming someone new - remembering who you have always been.'
Keep suggestions tied to the client's stated goal and their own keywords.
check: At least two permissive openers used (might/perhaps/may)
At least one presupposition delivered smoothly
Embedded command marked with voice drop and slight pause
Truism chain (3 truths + suggestion) delivered
Say-See-Feel arc complete for the main suggestion
Future-pace placed in a specific scene from their life
Suggestions used the client's own keywords
Unhurried delivery with the permissive coda

drills.name: Inferred Metaphor & Guided Imagery Design
prompter: Metaphor structure: isomorphic (parallel structure to the client's situation, not identical).
Elements: protagonist + challenge + resource + transformation + new normal.
Nature metaphors: tree (roots=foundation, branches=growth), river (flow around obstacles), seed (dormant potential).
Journey metaphors: path through a forest (dark to light), mountain climb (effort to vista), ocean crossing.
Transformation metaphors: caterpillar/butterfly, ice melting to water, dawn after night.
Multisensory: paint with all senses - what they see, hear, feel, smell in the scene.
Embed the therapeutic message: the protagonist's resolution mirrors the client's desired change.
The leaf and blade of grass (Kappasinian): leaf twists free, glides down, rests at the root; blade of grass persevered through its own motivation - 'the same way YOU are motivated.'
Let the metaphor breathe - silence between images lets the subconscious do its work.
Close: 'carry these feelings forward into the days ahead.'
check: Metaphor was isomorphic to the client's situation
All five elements present (protagonist, challenge, resource, transformation, new normal)
At least three senses engaged (visual + two others)
Therapeutic message embedded within the narrative
Pacing allowed silence between key images
Metaphor resolution mirrored the client's desired outcome
Closing carried the feelings forward

drills.name: 7 ± 2 Overload Induction
prompter: Frame: 'allow yourself to be as comfortable as you want to be, listening to the sound of my voice.'
Stack item 1: breathing - 'concentrating on your breathing, slowly and steadily.'
Stack item 2: self-image - 'imagine how comfortable you might look while relaxing in that chair.'
Stack item 3: head weight - 'noticing the weight of your head against the back of the chair.'
Stack item 4: ambient sound - 'while listening to the sounds in the room.'
Stack item 5: feet - 'notice the way your feet feel on the floor.'
Stack item 6: arms - 'perhaps how your arms feel.'
Stack item 7: temperature - 'adding an awareness of the temperature of the room.'
Stack item 8: eyes - 'and how your eyes feel while you're thinking about all those other things.'
Recap all 9 rapidly: voice, breathing, head weight, self-image, temperature, feet, arms, music, eyes.
Collapse: 'And now you can think how good it will feel when you simply allow yourself to think of only the most important thing of all...'
Single focus: '...how relaxed you can be now. No need to think anything at all. Nobody wanting anything. Nothing for you to do except to... relax.'
Keep a cheat sheet of all 9 items visible - if you lose track, that's fine, the confusion IS the mechanism.
check: At least 7 sensory items stacked before the collapse
Items added one at a time (not dumped all at once)
Recap listed items rapidly to create overload pressure
Collapse to single focus was smooth and inviting
Relief framing used ('how good it will feel to think of only one thing')
Permissive language throughout (no direct commands)
Pace was unhurried during stacking, then slightly faster at recap
Ended with clear relaxation anchor

drills.name: Ericksonian Confusion with Levitation
prompter: Frame: 'I'm not going to ask you to do anything uncomfortable. This is a learning process.'
Conscious/subconscious split: 'the conscious mind will hear the words and the subconscious mind will make the choices.'
Hand observation: 'look at your two hands - you may see similarities, or perhaps differences.'
Left/right bind: 'you may choose the left hand - perhaps that is the RIGHT choice for you. Or the right hand - the other will be the only one LEFT.'
Subconscious choice: 'your subconscious mind knows which of those two hands is lighter. Your conscious mind may be aware of the choices... or perhaps it is not.'
Lightness build: 'the feeling of lightness may start as a simple physical awareness of the difference between those hands.'

drills.name: PHS Re-Hypnosis (Script #5)
prompter: After suggestions are complete, count client OUT of hypnosis (0-5, eyes open, wide awake).
Let client orient briefly - check in: 'How do you feel?'
Frame the WHY: 'I am going to teach your mind to enter this state on its own — a tool for between sessions. Also confirms the PHS is installed.'
Now re-induce using the PHS: have them stare at fingernail of right index finger, paying attention to pulse.
Frame: 'I will say some phrases and you will repeat them back to me out loud.'
Guide them through the self-count: 'I will now enter the state of hypnosis... for reasons of deep relaxation and self-control.'
'I will count from five down to zero. With each count I will become more deeply relaxed. When I reach zero, I will go deep asleep.'
Client repeats each phrase, then counts: Five (breathing)... Four (eyelids heavy)... Three (muscles relaxing)...
Two (arms, legs, body deeply relaxed)... One (eyelids closing, rhythmic breathing)...
Zero - Deep Sleep! (snap or touch forehead).
Immediately repeat the PHS again to reinforce: 'Each and every time I suggest the words Deep Sleep...'
This proves to the client (and you) that the PHS is installed and working.

script: [After the suggestion phase is complete, count the client out of hypnosis: 0-1-2-3-4-5, eyes open, wide awake.]
[Allow the client to orient briefly.] Welcome back. How do you feel? Take a moment.

Now I am going to do something that may seem unusual. I am going to teach your mind to enter this state on its own — quickly and easily. This is a tool you will use between sessions, and it also confirms that the connection we have built today is solid. Ready?
Now I would like you to stare directly at the fingernail of your right index finger, while paying attention to your pulse.
All your attention is right there on that fingernail. Taking a deep breath now.
In a moment I will say some phrases and you will repeat them back to me out loud. Everything I say, you will say after I have said it. Ready?
Repeat after me: I will now enter the state of hypnosis. [Client repeats.]
For reasons of deep relaxation and self-control. [Client repeats.]
I will count from five down to zero. [Client repeats.]
And with each count I will become more deeply relaxed. [Client repeats.]
When I reach zero, I will go deep asleep. [Client repeats.]
Five — I begin to feel my breathing growing deep, gentle, and rhythmic. [Client repeats.]
Four — I begin to feel heaviness in my eyelids, as I become drowsier and sleepier. [Client repeats.]
Three — I begin to feel every muscle, nerve, and fiber in my body relaxing, deeply relaxing. [Client repeats.]
Two — my arms, my legs, my entire body are now deeply relaxed. [Client repeats.]
One — my eyelids closing, breathing becoming more rhythmic, I am deeply relaxed. [Client repeats.]
Zero — Deep Sleep! [Snap.]

Each and every time I suggest the words Deep Sleep to you, for the purpose of hypnosis and with your permission, you will enter this state of hypnosis very quickly, calmly, and deeply, and the physical body will relax.

drills.name: Depth Assessment & Deepener Selection
prompter: Read the depth signs: hypnoidal (up-down REM), cataleptic (side-to-side), somnambulism (whites showing).
If hypnoidal: client needs more deepening - add another round of deepeners.
If cataleptic: good working depth - proceed to prog relax or suggestions.
If somnambulistic: excellent depth - note for session record; proceed carefully.
Emotional clients may feel light but be deep - trust the eye signs, not their report.
Physical clients usually show depth clearly - watch for body stillness and breathing rate.
Choose the next deepener based on what the client has responded to best so far.
Decision point: stay in chair for more desk deepeners, or transition to recliner for prog relax.

script: [Observe the client's eyes beneath closed lids to assess depth.]
Hypnoidal (light): eyes moving up-and-down or showing REM-like flutter. Client needs additional deepening.
Cataleptic (medium): eyes moving side-to-side beneath the lids. Good working depth — proceed to progressive relaxation or suggestions.
Somnambulistic (deep): eyes rolled upward, whites may be visible. Excellent depth — note for session record.
[Remember: Emotional clients may report feeling light or like 'nothing happened' but may actually be in a deep state. Trust the eye signs, not their subjective report.]
[Physical clients typically display depth clearly through visible body stillness and slowed breathing rate.]
[Decision point: stay in the chair for additional desk-based deepeners, or transition to the recliner for progressive relaxation.]

drills.name: Suggestibility Testing
prompter: Purpose: determine E/P suggestibility BEFORE the induction. This sets the lane for the entire session.
Finger-spread test: hand up, fingers straight, stare at middle finger, take a breath — on exhale, fingers begin to separate.
Watch the spread pattern: Physical clients spread fast and wide; Emotional clients spread slowly with more internal processing.
Heavy/Light test (brief version): arms out, book on one palm, balloons on the other — observe which direction dominates.
Handwriting analysis (optional): have them write a sentence. Pressure, slant, and letter formation reveal suggestibility.
Score the result: assign an E/P percentage (e.g., 72% Physical). This determines your language, pace, and tone for the session.
Record the E/P score. Share the result with the client — builds credibility and buy-in.

script: Now before we begin the hypnosis, I would like to do a quick assessment. This helps me understand how your mind processes information, so I can tailor everything specifically to you.
I would like you to raise your hand and place the palm in front of your face, about ten inches away, with your fingers pointing straight up and above eye level.
Now stare at your middle finger. Take a deep breath, and on the exhale, your fingers will begin to separate. Separating, wider and wider, further and further apart.
[Observe: Physical suggestible — fingers spread quickly and visibly. Emotional suggestible — fingers spread slowly, may need more repetition, more internal processing before movement.]
Good. You can relax your hand. Now let me do one more quick test.
Put both arms out in front of you at shoulder height. One palm up, the other with the thumb pointing to the ceiling. Close your eyes.
Imagine a heavy book on the open palm, pressing it down. And on the other thumb, imagine a bunch of helium balloons pulling it up. Just let your arms respond naturally.
[Pause 10-15 seconds. Observe which arm moves more and how quickly. Physical clients show fast, visible arm movement. Emotional clients show subtle, slow shifts.]
Good. You can relax both arms. Thank you.

[Based on the results, assign E/P percentage. Share with the client:] Based on what I am seeing, your mind processes information in a way that is about [X]% physical and [Y]% emotional. This is neither good nor bad — it simply tells me the best way to communicate with your subconscious mind today.
